description: Per-variation costume material pattern table: eight parallel arrays (P1-P8) of material instance names that a character material controller shows or hides depending on the selected material pattern index.

ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export), typically a variation ID (CP_xxx_yy). UGameCharacterMaterialController::SetMaterialPattern resolves the owner's current CharacterVariation row, reads its Id_CharacterMaterial and finds this row in CharacterMaterialDataTables (DTM +0x490). A null Row pointer passed explicitly (as for shikigami capture) bypasses the lookup.

MaterialName_P1.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 1 (index 0).
MaterialName_P1.technical: TArray<FName>, first of eight parallel arrays. SetMaterialPattern accepts Pattern in [0,7] (range-checked as a float); index 0 selects this array as the shown pattern. All eight arrays are first applied with bShow=false in stable sorted order, then the selected array with bShow=true; None names are skipped. A name is only acted upon if it is present in the controller's harvested Outline/RimParameters map, in which case ShowMaterialSections toggles that material's mesh sections.

MaterialName_P2.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 2 (index 1).
MaterialName_P2.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 1; otherwise hidden by the same hide-first/show-selected pass. Exported slots contain names like MI_CP_050_00_Hair_P2 and None padding.

MaterialName_P3.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 3 (index 2).
MaterialName_P3.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 2; hidden otherwise. Behavior identical to the other pattern arrays; arrays can repeat the same material names across patterns.

MaterialName_P4.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 4 (index 3).
MaterialName_P4.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 3; hidden otherwise.

MaterialName_P5.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 5 (index 4).
MaterialName_P5.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 4; hidden otherwise.

MaterialName_P6.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 6 (index 5).
MaterialName_P6.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 5; hidden otherwise.

MaterialName_P7.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 7 (index 6).
MaterialName_P7.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 6; hidden otherwise.

MaterialName_P8.simple: Material-instance names belonging to costume pattern 8 (index 7).
MaterialName_P8.technical: TArray<FName> selected when Pattern == 7; hidden otherwise. Exported P8 arrays are commonly all None, i.e. no extra material sections for the last pattern.

notes: Export contains 27 rows, each with eight material-name arrays of six slots. Missing variation material references simply leave the controller's default pattern state.

Pattern is an int32 in [0,7]; values outside that range return without changing AppliedPattern. The controller's material harvesting (Outline/Rim parameters) must have run, otherwise names cannot be mapped to mesh sections.

Both battle characters and capture spawns call SetMaterialPattern; capture SituationOverview poses choose the pattern from the variation parameter rather than the slot. Shikigami passes an explicit row pointer (null), so CharacterMaterial is not used for shikigami.
No per-locale or numbered-shard variants exist in the export; no claim about Blueprint-only consumers or uncooked assets.

usages.detail: SetMaterialPattern resolves the row when no explicit row is supplied.
Switches P1-P8 arrays into the selected pattern and toggles matching mesh sections.
Capture setup calls SetMaterialPattern with a slot or variation parameter pattern.
